translated:
काठमांडू, मिथिला मिरर: नेपालक मधेश प्रदेशमे भेल झड़पमे गुरुवारके एक किशोरके मृत्यु भेल अछि, जाहिमे अहि सप्ताहक प्रारंभमे पड़ोसी कोशी प्रान्तके भारतक सीमामे स्थित सुनसरी जिल्लामे भेल साम्प्रदायिक हिंसाक बाद एक गोटेके मृत्यु भेल आ कतेको गोटे घायल भेलाक बाद अधिकारी बेसी क्षेत्रमे निषेधाज्ञा बढ़ाओल गेल अछि ।

मधेश प्रदेशके सिरहा जिल्लाके गोलबजार बजारमे भेल झडपमे किशोरके मृत्यु भेल अछि, तहिना सुनसरी हिंसामे घायल एक गोटेके कोशी प्रदेशमे मृत्यु भेल अधिकारीसब जनौलक अछि ।

एहि स नेपाल के दू प्रांत कोशी आ मधेश, दुनू प्रांत बिहार स सटल अछि, सप्ताह भरि चलि रहल साम्प्रदायिक हिंसा मे मृतक के संख्या तीन भ गेल अछि।

मधेश प्रदेशके धनुषा, सिराहा आ वीरगंज जिल्लाके किछु भागमे बृहस्पतिदिन अनिश्चितकालीन निषेधाज्ञा लगाओल गेल अछि त सुनसरी जिल्लामे सोमदिन सर्वप्रथम निषेधाज्ञा लगाओल गेल छल ओ अनिश्चित काल धरि लागू रहल अछि ।

सुनसरी जिल्लाके देवानगंज ग्रामीण नगरपालिकाके कपतानगुञ्ज क्षेत्रमे रविदिन दुटा धार्मिक समुदायके उत्सवके क्रममे झगड़ामे झगडैत समूहके तितर-बितर करबाक लेल प्रहरी गोलीबारी केने एक गोटेके मृत्यु भेल आ सुरक्षाकर्मीसहित एक दर्जनसँ बेसी जना घायल भेल अछि ।

बृहस्पतिदिन सिराहा जिलाक गोलबजारक समीप तुलसीपुरक १५ वर्षीय गणेश यादव दू समूहक बीच भेल झड़प मे गंभीर रूप सँ घायल भेल अछि । स्थानीय अस्पतालमे ईलाजके क्रममे यादवके मृत्यु भेल प्रहरी जनौलक अछि ।

गोलबाजार क्षेत्रमे अनिश्चितकालीन निषेधाज्ञाके आदेश बृहस्पतिदिन लहान नगरपालिकामे बढाओल गेल जिल्ला प्रशासनके अनुसार । ई घटना गोलबाजार क्षेत्र मँ अलग-अलग समूह द्वारा आयोजित हिंसक विरोध प्रदर्शन के दौरान घटित होलै, जहां आंदोलनकारी नँ एगो शॉपिंग मॉल मँ भी आग लगाय देलकै ।

सुनसरी जिल्लाके देवानगंज ग्रामीण नगरपालिकामे साम्प्रदायिक झड़पमे गम्भीर घायल भेल जयप्रकाश मेहताके विराटनगरके न्यूरो अस्पतालमे उपचारके क्रममे बृहस्पतिदिन मृत्यु भेल ग्रामीण नगरपालिकाके अध्यक्ष बेचन मेहता जनौलक अछि ।

मेहता देवानगंजमे रविदिन भेल साम्प्रदायिक हिंसामे मारल गेल दुनू व्यक्तिके नेपाली १० लाख रुपैयाक मुआवजा देबाक घोषणा केलन्हि ।

सम्बन्धित घटनाक्रममे मधेश प्रदेशके पर्साके जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय एहतियातके रुपमे वीरगंज महानगरपालिकाके कुछ भागमे निषेधात्मक आदेश जारी करले बा ।

सुनसरी मे दू धार्मिक समूहक बीच झड़प के बाद भेल हिंसा के जवाब मे किछु लोक के प्रदर्शन के बाद प्रशासन निषेधात्मक आदेश जारी केलक अछि।

डीएओ पर्सा द्वारा जारी सूचना मे कहल गेल अछि जे, पूर्व मे प्रतिमा चौक, पश्चिम मे तिलाबे पुल, उत्तर मे गंडक चौक आ बिहार मे रक्सौल क सीमावर्ती वीरगंज क दक्षिण मे शंकराचार्य गेट क बीच क्षेत्र मे इ निषेधात्मक आदेश लागू छल।

निषेधात्मक आदेश के तहत पांच या ओहि सं बेसी लोक के सभा पर रोक अछि, कोनो तरहक प्रदर्शन, धरना, जनसभा या बैसार के अनुमति नहिं अछि. अधिकारी सब कहलनि जे, गुरुवार के सांझ 5 बजे सं शुक्रदिन भोर 6 बजे तक निषेधात्मक आदेश लागू रहत।

अहिसँ पहिने बृहस्पतिदिन धनुषाके विभिन्न भागमे लक्ष्मीनिया हाटबजार, बेलौनी रोड, नगराईन नगरपालिका, दूधमती पुल आ जनकपुर सहित साम्प्रदायिक तनावके कारण एहतियातके रुपमे दुपहर ३:३० बजेसँ अनिश्चितकालके लेल निषेधाज्ञा लगाओल गेल धनुषाके सहायक प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी भूदेव झा जानकारी देलनि ।

सुनसरी जिला मे पहिल बेर सोमदिन लगाओल गेल कर्फ्यू अनिश्चित काल तक बढ़ैत रहल, हालांकि स्थिति मे धीरे-धीरे सुधार भ रहल छल।

सुनसरी के सहायक मुख्य जिला अधिकारी पोशन लामिछाने गुरुवार के सुनसरी जिला के सुरक्षा स्थिति में धीरे-धीरे सुधार भ रहल अछि, मुदा जिला प्रशासन स्थिति पर नियंत्रण के लेल पूर्व-पश्चिम राजमार्ग सहित 10 क्षेत्र में कर्फ्यू बढ़ा देलक।

नेपाली कांग्रेसक बसना थापा आ श्रम संस्कृति पार्टीक ओरेन राय सहित कतेको विधायक बृहस्पतिदिन संसदमे बजैत सुनसरी सहित दक्षिण नेपाल जिल्लामे बढैत तनाव दिस सरकारक ध्यान आकर्षित कएलन्हि ।

प्रधानमंत्री बलेन्द्र शाह के अध्यक्षता में दिन में राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा परिषद (एनएससी) के 43वीं बैठक भेल, जे देश के समग्र कानून व्यवस्था के स्थिति पर केंद्रित छल. आधिकारिक सूत्र कहलनि जे, बैसार मे राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा के व्यापक समीक्षा कायल गेल आ सुनसरी मे हाल के अशांति के मूल्यांकन सेहो कायल गेल।

राष्ट्रपति रामचन्द्र पौडेल, स्थिति पर गहरी चिन्ता व्यक्त करैत सामाजिक, धार्मिक आ साम्प्रदायिक सौहार्द आ राष्ट्रीय एकता कायम रखबाक लेल सब गोटे स अपील केलनि।

राष्ट्रपति पौडेल विज्ञप्ति जारी कए कहलनि जे, बहुसांस्कृतिक, बहुजातीय आ बहुजातीय समाजक विशेषता वाला देश मे नेपाली जनताक पहिचान आ परम्पराक विशिष्ट विशेषता अछि, सद्भावना, मेलमिलाप आ भाईचारा।

ओ संबंधित एजेंसी स सेहो आह्वान केलथि जे ओ एहि घटना क तटस्थ आ तथ्यात्मक जांच क अपराधी क खिलाफ कड़ा कार्रवाई करथि।

भारत के बिहार के सीमा पर दक्षिण पूर्वी नेपाल में स्थित सुनसरी दुनु देश के बीच एकटा महत्वपूर्ण पारगमन आ वाणिज्यिक गलियारा अछि। मधेश आ कोशी प्रांतक दक्षिणी जिलाक सीमा सेहो बिहारक संग साझा अछि। पीटीआई

title: Former President Bhandari urges for maintaining social harmony - The Rising Nepal
description: Former President Bhandari urges for maintaining social harmony  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
Kathmandu, July 30: Former President Biddya Devi Bhandari has urged to exercise optimum restraint in the present sensitive situation.

She appealed to one and all for not flowing fake news and provocative expression of any type.

Issuing a press release today, former President Bhandari expressed serious concern over the recent communal tensions and violent incidents in some parts of the country, including Sunsari.

She noted news of people losing their lives and some others being injured in these incidents has deeply saddened her.

Bhandari offered heartfelt condolences to the deceased and wished for the speedy recovery of the injured. “Nepal is a nation with diversity in ethnicity, language, religion, and culture. Unity amid diversity, mutual respect, and social harmony are Nepal’s intrinsic identity and pride, and it is everyone’s shared responsibility to preserve them."

She further stated the priceless traditions that our ancestors built and have proudly maintained for generations will not be allowed to weaken under any circumstances,” her statement said.

Since a sustainable solution to such problems is only possible through the rule of law, mutual trust, and continuous dialogue, the former President noted, urging the Nepal government, relevant administrative bodies, and security agencies to conduct a fair, transparent, and credible investigation into the incidents and hold the guilty accountable according to the law. (RSS)

काठमांडू, ३० जुलाई : पूर्व राष्ट्रपति बिद्या देवी भण्डारी वर्तमान संवेदनशील स्थिति मे इष्टतम संयम करबाक आग्रह केने छथि ।

ओ एक आ सब स अपील केलनि जे कोनो तरहक फेक न्यूज आ भड़काऊ अभिव्यक्ति नहि बहय।

आइ एकटा प्रेस विज्ञप्ति जारी करैत पूर्व राष्ट्रपति भण्डारी सुनसरी सहित देशक किछु भाग मे हाल मे साम्प्रदायिक तनाव आ हिंसक घटना पर गंभीर चिंता व्यक्त केलनि।

हुनी नोट करलकै कि ई घटना मँ लोगऽ के जान आरू कुछ लोगऽ के घायल होय के खबर हुनका बहुत दुखी करी देल॑ छै ।

भंडारी मृतक के हार्दिक संवेदना व्यक्त करैत घायल के शीघ्र ठीक होयबाक कामना केलनि। "नेपाल जातीयता, भाषा, धर्म, आरू संस्कृति के विविधता वाला राष्ट्र छै । विविधता के बीच एकता, आपसी सम्मान, आरू सामाजिक सौहार्द नेपाल के आंतरिक पहचान आरू गौरव छै, आरू एकरा संरक्षित करना सब के साझा जिम्मेदारी छै।"

हुनी आगू कहलकै कि जे अमूल्य परंपरा हमरऽ पूर्वज न॑ बनयने छेलै आरू पीढ़ी-दर-पीढ़ी गर्व स॑ कायम रखन॑ छै, ओकरा कोनो भी हालत म॑ कमजोर नै होबै देलऽ जैतै ।’’ हुनकऽ बयान म॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

चूँकि एहन समस्या के स्थायी समाधान कानून के राज, आपसी विश्वास, आ निरंतर संवाद के माध्यम स मात्र संभव अछि, पूर्व राष्ट्रपति नेपाल सरकार, संबंधित प्रशासनिक निकाय, आ सुरक्षा एजेंसी स आग्रह करैत नोट केलथि जे ओ घटना के निष्पक्ष, पारदर्शी, आ विश्वसनीय जांच करथि आ दोषी के कानून के अनुसार जवाबदेह बनाबथि। (आर एस एस) २.

title: Nepal enforces curfew amid escalating religious tensions - Yahoo
description: Nepal enforces curfew amid escalating religious tensions  Yahoo

full_article:
Nepali authorities have enforced a curfew in several places across the country's southern plain amid escalating religious tensions between Hindu and Muslim communities, police said on Thursday.

Curfews have been imposed in parts of Siraha, Sunsari and Dhanusa districts bordering the Indian state of Bihar, where religious tensions have been growing in recent days, according to Nepal Police spokesman Abi Narayan Kafle.

"Nepal Police is working with the unified security forces to prevent vandalism, arson and communal tension," Kafle said.

Kafle said that at least two people have died since Sunday, when violence erupted after Hindu pilgrims were attacked in Sunsari district of eastern Nepal while heading to a temple. He said that both victims were shot on Sunday.

One died on the same day, while the other, who had been receiving treatment, succumbed to his injuries at the hospital Thursday.

It remains unclear who fired the shots, as no security agency has taken responsibility.

President Ramchandra Paudel has expressed concern over the situation and appealed for social, religious and ethnic harmony.

Separately, Prime Minister Balendra Shah, in an address to the nation, pledged a transparent investigation into the incidents, assured medical care for the injured, and vowed action against those spreading hate and misinformation.

Nepal, a country of 29 million people, is roughly around 81% Hindu. Other religious minorities include Buddhists, Muslims and Christians.

title: Nepal PM appeals for calm as communal violence kills three in border districts - indiatoday.in
description: Nepal PM appeals for calm as communal violence kills three in border districts  indiatoday.in
publisher.title: indiatoday.in
full_article:
Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Thursday appealed for calm and harmony after three people died in communal violence in border districts, as authorities expanded curfew restrictions to more areas. In a televised address, Shah said the government would ensure a neutral and transparent investigation into the violence and hold those responsible accountable.

The unrest, which began in Sunsari district of Koshi province and later spread to parts of neighbouring Madhesh province, has led to curfews, prohibitory orders and the deployment of security forces. The government has also stepped up political and administrative measures to contain the situation and ease tensions.

advertisement ❮❯

Read Full Story

The violence first broke out on Sunday night in the Kaptangunj area of Devganj rural municipality in Sunsari district when members of two communities, who were separately organising programmes, clashed over the use of loudspeakers and the display of religious flags. On Thursday, the violence spread to Golbazar market in Siraha district of Madhesh province, where a teenager died in the clashes. Officials also said one person injured in the Sunsari violence died in Koshi province.

An indefinite curfew was imposed in parts of Dhanusa, Siraha and Birgunj districts of Madhesh province on Thursday, while the curfew in Sunsari district, first imposed on Monday, remained in force. Shah said the government was looking into the incidents in Sunsari's Devganj and parts of Siraha with the "utmost seriousness and sensitivity". He said health authorities had been instructed to ensure prompt treatment for the injured. He also said the home ministry had formed an investigation committee and promised that the inquiry would be impartial and transparent. Security forces have been deployed to prevent further violence and restore normalcy, he added.

According to the Prime Minister, the home minister travelled to the affected areas to oversee the security situation, while the National Security Council reviewed the unrest and took necessary decisions. Shah said an all-party meeting had been convened in Kathmandu and dialogue was continuing to ease tensions. He also urged the public not to spread rumours, misinformation or hate speech through social media or other platforms.

In a related development, the District Administration Office of Parsa in Madhesh province issued prohibitory orders in parts of Birgunj Metropolitan City as a precaution after demonstrations by some people in response to the violence in Sunsari. The restrictions covered the area between Pratima Chowk in the east, Tilabe Bridge in the west, Gandak Chowk in the north and Shankaracharya Gate in the south of Birgunj, which borders Raxaul in Bihar. Under the orders, gatherings of five or more people were banned, and no demonstration, sit-in, public meeting or meeting was allowed. Officials said the order would remain in effect from 5 pm on Thursday till 6 am on Friday. Earlier in the day, various parts of Dhanusa, including Laxminia Hatbazaar, Belauni Road, Nagarain Municipality, Dudhmati bridge and Janakpur, were placed under curfew from 3.30 pm for an indefinite period as a precautionary measure due to communal tensions, Assistant Chief District Officer of Dhanusha Bhudev Jha said. Sunsari's Assistant Chief District Officer Poshan Lamichhane said the security situation in the district was gradually improving, but the administration had extended the curfew to 10 areas, including the East-West Highway, to control the situation.

Several lawmakers, including Basna Thapa of Nepali Congress and Oren Rai of Shram Sanskriti Party, raised the issue of growing tension in southern Nepal districts, including Sunsari, in Parliament on Thursday. President Ramchandra Paudel expressed deep concern and appealed for social, religious and communal harmony and national unity. "Goodwill, reconciliation and brotherhood are the unique features of the identity and tradition of the Nepalese people, in a country characterised by a multi-cultural, multi-ethnic and multi-racial society," President Paudel said in a statement. He also called on the agencies concerned to take stern action against the culprits through a neutral and factual investigation. Overall, the government has responded with curfews, security deployment, talks and an inquiry, as Nepal seeks to contain the violence that began in Sunsari and spread to parts of Madhesh.

कोशी प्रांत के सुनसरी जिला स शुरू भेल आ बाद में पड़ोसी मधेश प्रांत के किछु हिस्सा में पसरल अशांति के कारण कर्फ्यू, निषेधात्मक आदेश आ सुरक्षा बल के तैनाती के कारण बनल अछि। सरकार एहि स्थिति कए रोकबा आ तनाव कम करबा लेल राजनीतिक आ प्रशासनिक उपाय सेहो तेज केलक अछि।

विज्ञापन ❮❯ २.

पूरा कहानी पढ़ें

सुनसरी जिला के देवगंज ग्रामीण नगरपालिका के कप्तानगुंज इलाका मे रविदिन राति मे पहिल बेर हिंसा भड़कल छल जखन अलग-अलग कार्यक्रम के आयोजन करय वाला दू समुदाय के सदस्य मे लाउडस्पीकर के प्रयोग आ धार्मिक झंडा के प्रदर्शन के ल क झड़प भेल छल. बृहस्पतिदिन मधेश प्रदेशके सिरहा जिल्लाके गोलबजार बजारमे हिंसा पसरल, जतहि झडपमे एक किशोरके मृत्यु भेल छल । अधिकारी सब इहो कहलनि जे, सुनसरी हिंसा मे घायल एक गोटे के कोशी प्रांत मे मौत भ गेल।

मधेश प्रदेशके धनुषा, सिराहा आ वीरगंज जिल्लाके किछु भागमे बृहस्पतिदिन अनिश्चितकालीन निषेधाज्ञा लगाओल गेल अछि, तहिना सुनसरी जिल्लामे सोमदिन पहिल बेर लगाओल गेल निषेधाज्ञा लागू रहल अछि । शाह नँ कहलकै कि सरकार सुनसरी के देवगंज आरू सिराहा के कुछ हिस्सा मँ घटित घटना के बारे मँ 'अत्यधिक गंभीरता आरू संवेदनशीलता' के साथ देखै छै । ओ कहलनि जे, स्वास्थ्य अधिकारी के निर्देश देल गेल अछि जे घायल के शीघ्र इलाज सुनिश्चित करय। संगहि ओ कहला जे गृह मंत्रालय जांच समिति बना कए जांच निष्पक्ष आ पारदर्शी हेबाक वादा केलक अछि। ओ आगू कहलनि जे, आओर हिंसा के रोकय आ सामान्य स्थिति बहाल करय लेल सुरक्षा बल के तैनाती कायल गेल अछि।

प्रधानमंत्री के अनुसार गृहमंत्री सुरक्षा स्थिति के देखरेख के लेल प्रभावित क्षेत्र के यात्रा केलनि, जखन कि राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा परिषद अशांति के समीक्षा केलक आ आवश्यक निर्णय लेलक। शाह काठमाण्डौमे सर्वदलीय बैसार बजाओल गेल आ तनाव कम करबाक लेल संवाद जारी रहल बतौलनि । संगहि ओ जनता स आग्रह केलथि जे सोशल मीडिया या अन्य प्लेटफॉर्म क माध्यम स अफवाह, गलत सूचना या नफरत क भाषण नहि फैलाबथि।

एहि सँ जुड़ल एकटा घटनाक्रम मे सुनसरी मे भेल हिंसाक प्रतिक्रिया मे किछु लोक द्वारा प्रदर्शन केलाक बाद एहतियात के तौर पर मधेश प्रदेश के पर्सा के जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय द्वारा वीरगंज महानगर के किछु भाग मे निषेधात्मक आदेश जारी कयल गेल अछि । एहि प्रतिबंध मे पूर्व मे प्रतिमा चौक, पश्चिम मे तिलाबे पुल, उत्तर मे गंडक चौक आ बिहार क रक्सौल स सटल वीरगंज क दक्षिण मे शंकराचार्य गेट क बीच क इलाका शामिल अछि। आदेश के तहत पांच या ओहि सं बेसी लोक के जुटान पर रोक लगा देल गेल छल, आओर कोनो तरहक प्रदर्शन, धरना, जनसभा या बैसार के अनुमति नहिं छल. अधिकारी कहलनि जे, ई आदेश गुरुवार के सांझ 5 बजे सं शुक्रदिन भोर 6 बजे तक लागू रहत। अहिसँ पहिने धनुषाके विभिन्न भागमे लक्ष्मीनिया हाटबजार, बेलौनी रोड, नगराईन नगरपालिका, दूधमती पुल आ जनकपुर सहित साम्प्रदायिक तनावके कारण एहतियातके रुपमे दुपहर ३.३० बजेसँ अनिश्चितकालके लेल निषेधाज्ञा लगाओल गेल धनुषाके सहायक प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी भूदेव झा जानकारी देलनि । सुनसरी के सहायक मुख्य जिला अधिकारी पोशन लामिछाने कहलनि जे, जिला के सुरक्षा स्थिति धीरे-धीरे सुधार भ रहल अछि, मुदा प्रशासन स्थिति पर नियंत्रण के लेल पूर्व-पश्चिम राजमार्ग सहित 10 क्षेत्र मे कर्फ्यू बढ़ा देलक अछि।

Kathmandu [Nepal], July 30 (ANI): Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Thursday appealed for unity, restraint and social harmony as violence in the southern plains of Nepal has claimed at least three lives. "I pay my heartfelt tribute to our citizens Jayaprakash Mehta, Om Prakash Mehta and Ganesh Yadav, who passed away in this tragic incident. I also express my deepest condolences to the bereaved families on behalf of the Government of Nepal. I wish a speedy recovery to all the citizens who were injured in the incident. Clear instructions have been given to the concerned health agencies to ensure that there is no shortage or delay in the treatment of the injured," he added. Advertisement googletag.cmd.push((function(){googletag.display("div-gpt-ad-1722694474562-0")})) The unrest in Sunsari began late Sunday night in Ward No. 3 of Dewanganj Rural Municipality after a dispute reportedly broke out between local groups over loud music during preparations for the Bol Bam pilgrimage to the Saptakoshi River. The confrontation quickly escalated into stone-pelting and violence, prompting police to intervene with batons, tear gas, warning shots and eventually live fire by the Armed Police Force. One person died on the spot from gunshot injuries, while several others were critically injured. Jayaprakash Mehta, who had sustained injuries in the violence, succumbed to his injuries on Thursday, taking the death toll to three. Announcing the formation of an investigation committee, Shah assured the public that the inquiry would be fair and transparent and that those responsible would face legal action. "As soon as the incident happened, all security agencies immediately reached the spot and made continuous efforts to normalise the situation, prevent further unpleasant incidents and maintain peace and security. The Ministry of Home Affairs has formed an investigation committee to conduct a fair investigation into the incident and take strict legal action against the culprits. I would like to assure everyone that this investigation will be completely fair and transparent. The government is committed to bringing whoever is responsible for the incident to justice," Shah said. He said that the government has adopted a multi-pronged approach to restore normalcy. An all-party meeting was convened at the central level, while continuous dialogue has been held with local representatives, civil society members, religious leaders, community representatives and social activists. "The Home Minister himself has already reached the spot to directly monitor the local situation, communicate with the affected parties, and further strengthen peace and security. In addition, a meeting of the National Security Council has been convened to seriously review the overall peace and security situation in the country and necessary decisions have been taken according to the situation," he said. In his four-and-a-half-minute televised address, Shah also appealed to citizens not to spread misinformation or inflammatory content. He urged people to refrain from circulating false or unverified information, rumours, hate speech or messages that could inflame inter-community tensions, and asked them to rely only on official information issued by government agencies. He also warned that action would be taken against those attempting to disrupt peace, spread chaos or undermine Nepal's long-standing traditions of tolerance and brotherhood. "The Constitution of Nepal has granted every citizen the fundamental right to follow their own religion, culture and traditions. The government is fully committed to fulfilling this constitutional obligation. Religion is the force that unites society and spreads love. No religion or culture in the world teaches violence, hatred and division. The essence of all religions is compassion, mercy, love and peace. Blaming an entire community for an unexpected and tragic incident in one part of the country and spreading the fire of revenge for it in other parts of the country cannot be justified or justified from any perspective," the Nepalese PM said. Concluding his address with a message delivered in both Nepali and Maithili, Shah called for collective efforts to restore peace and strengthen national unity. "Our history is a witness that even in the most difficult and difficult situations, mutual unity, tolerance and conscience have become our greatest strength. We all have to play the role of responsible citizens and remove the clouds of unrest that have hung over this beautiful and peaceful Nepali sky. We, the common citizens, civil society, religious communities, all respected leaders, all political parties and responsible media, are making a heartfelt appeal to the government to exercise patience and restraint and maintain peace, harmony, brotherhood and national unity," he added. The government's response comes amid curfews, prohibitory orders and heightened security deployments in Sunsari, Siraha, Janakpur and Parsa districts. Since Sunday, protests and tensions have spread, raising concerns over broader communal friction in the region bordering India. title: Non-Resident Nepali Association Expresses Concern Over Sunsari Incidents, Urges Peaceful Resolution - english.ratopati.com
description: Non-Resident Nepali Association Expresses Concern Over Sunsari Incidents, Urges Peaceful Resolution  english.ratopati.com
publisher.title: english.ratopati.com
full_article:
Kathmandu. The Non-Resident Nepali Association (NRNA) has expressed deep concern over the incidents in places like Devangunj, Siraha, Sunsari and urged the government and all stakeholders to maintain social harmony and seek a peaceful resolution to the problem.

In a press statement issued by the association's president Dr. Hemraj Sharma on Thursday, condolences were expressed to the citizens who lost their lives in the incident, and sympathy was extended to the bereaved families. It has also been requested from the Government of Nepal to immediately arrange for the necessary health services, treatment and support for effective treatment of the injured, wishing them a speedy, full and successful recovery.

The statement mentioned that social, religious, ethnic harmony, tolerance, reconciliation and brotherhood are the identity of Nepal, and any kind of violence, malice, hatred or division will weaken the nation and society.

NRNA has urged the government, political parties, civil society, local communities and all stakeholders to seek a peaceful resolution to the problem through dialogue, cooperation, restraint and mutual understanding to normalize the current difficult situation as soon as possible, ensure the security of citizens' lives and property, maintain social harmony, and re-establish peace, security and trust in society.
translated:
काठमांडू। अनिवासी नेपाली संघ देवनगुंज, सिराहा, सुनसरी आदि स्थानमे घटित घटना पर गहींर चिन्ता व्यक्त करैत सरकार आ समस्त सरोकारवाला स सामाजिक सौहार्द कायम राखब आ समस्याक शान्तिपूर्ण समाधान ताकब आग्रह केने अछि ।

एसोसिएशन के अध्यक्ष डॉ. हेमराज शर्मा द्वारा गुरुवार के जारी प्रेस विज्ञप्ति में घटना में जान गंवाबै वाला नागरिक के प्रति शोक व्यक्त करलौ गेलौ छै, आरू शोक संतप्त परिवार के प्रति सहानुभूति व्यक्त करलौ गेलौ छै । नेपाल सरकारसँ सेहो आग्रह कएल गेल अछि जे घायल लोकनिक शीघ्र, पूर्ण आ सफल स्वस्थ्य हेबाक कामना करैत तत्काल आवश्यक स्वास्थ्य सेवा, उपचार आ प्रभावी उपचारक लेल सहयोगक व्यवस्था कयल जाय ।

विज्ञप्ति मे सामाजिक, धार्मिक, जातीय सौहार्द, सहिष्णुता, मेलमिलाप आ भाईचारा नेपालक पहिचान अछि, आ कोनो तरहक हिंसा, दुर्भावना, घृणा वा विभाजन राष्ट्र आ समाज कमजोर करत से उल्लेख कएल गेल अछि ।

एनआरएनए सरकार, राजनीतिक दल, नागरिक समाज, स्थानीय समुदाय आरू सब हितधारक स॑ आग्रह करल॑ छै कि वर्तमान कठिन परिस्थिति क॑ जल्द स॑ जल्द सामान्य करै लेली, नागरिकऽ के जीवन आरू संपत्ति के सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित करै लेली, सामाजिक सौहार्द कायम रखै लेली, आरू समाज म॑ शांति, सुरक्षा आरू विश्वास क॑ पुनः स्थापित करै लेली संवाद, सहयोग, संयम आरू आपसी समझदारी के माध्यम स॑ समस्या के शांतिपूर्ण समाधान खोजै के कोशिश करलऽ जाय ।

title: Nepal PM urges calm after unrest leaves 3 dead - CP24
description: Nepal PM urges calm after unrest leaves 3 dead  CP24
publisher.title: CP24
full_article:
KATHMANDU, Nepal - Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Thursday appealed for calm after clashes between Hindu and Muslim groups in the country’s south sparked unrest that has left three people dead.

Shah, who has kept a low profile since being elected in March, broke his silence to deliver his first address to the nation, calling on his countrymen to be “responsible citizens and remove the clouds of unrest.”

The violence began late Sunday in a village in the southern Sunsari district, which borders India, after an argument over loud music and the use of religious flags during a Hindu procession, according to officials.

Police opened fire to disperse the crowd, said local official Poshan Lamichhane. Two men died in the unrest, according to police spokesman Abi Narayan Kafle.

Authorities are investigating the deaths and have imposed a curfew in Sunsari and neighbouring districts to prevent further clashes.

A third man was killed Thursday in the nearby Siraha district during a demonstration that took place while the curfew was in force.

“I, on behalf of the government, sincerely appeal to the citizens, civil society, religious communities, all respected leaders, all political parties and responsible media, to exercise patience and restrain and maintain peace, harmony, brotherhood and national unity,” Shah said in a video address.

Nepal, a secular republic where more than 80 per cent of the population is Hindu, has seen tensions flare occasionally in the southern plains, where sizeable Hindu and Muslim communities live side by side.

In his address, Shah vowed that the investigation would be “completely fair and transparent.”

“The government is committed to bringing to justice whoever is responsible for the incident,” he said.

Kafle, the police official, said efforts were being made to restore order.

“We have kept all police officials in the field on alert and are trying to protect public property and prevent any conflicting situation with minimal use of force,” he told AFP.

अधिकारी सब के अनुसार भारत के सीमा स सटल दक्षिणी सुनसरी जिला के एकटा गाम में रविदिन देर राति हिन्दू जुलूस के दौरान जोरदार संगीत आ धार्मिक झंडा के प्रयोग के ल क बहस के बाद हिंसा शुरू भेल।

भीड़ के तितर-बितर करय लेल पुलिस गोली चला देलक स्थानीय अधिकारी पोशन लामिछाने जानकारी देलनि। अशांति मे दू गोटेक मृत्यु भेल पुलिस प्रवक्ता अबी नारायण काफ्लेक अनुसार।

अधिकारी सब मौत के जांच क रहल अछि आओर सुनसरी आओर पड़ोसी जिला मे आओर झड़प नहि होए ताहि लेल कर्फ्यू लगा देने अछि.

बृहस्पतिदिन नजदीकी सिराहा जिला मे कर्फ्यू लागू रहला के दौरान भेल प्रदर्शन के दौरान तेसर आदमी के मौत भ गेल।

शाह न॑ वीडियो संबोधन म॑ कहलकै कि हम्में सरकार के तरफ स॑ नागरिक, नागरिक समाज, धार्मिक समुदाय, सब सम्मानित नेता, सब राजनीतिक दल आरू जिम्मेदार मीडिया स॑ ईमानदारी स॑ अपील करै छियै कि धैर्य के प्रयोग करी क॑ शांति, सौहार्द, भाईचारा आरू राष्ट्रीय एकता क॑ संयमित करी क॑ कायम रखै ।

धर्मनिरपेक्ष गणराज्य नेपाल, जहाँ ८० प्रतिशत स॑ अधिक आबादी हिन्दू छै, दक्षिणी मैदानऽ म॑ बीच-बीच म॑ तनाव पैदा होय रहलऽ छै, जहां बड़ऽ-बड़ऽ हिन्दू आरू मुस्लिम समुदाय एक-दूसरा के साथ रह॑ छै ।

अपनऽ संबोधन म॑ शाह न॑ प्रण लेलकै कि जांच “पूरी तरह स॑ निष्पक्ष आरू पारदर्शी” होतै ।

ओ कहलनि जे, सरकार एहि घटना के लेल जे कियो जिम्मेदार अछि ओकरा कानून के सामने लाबय लेल प्रतिबद्ध अछि।

पुलिस अधिकारी काफ्ले कहलनि जे, व्यवस्था बहाल करबाक प्रयास भ रहल अछि।

ओ एएफपी स कहला जे हम मैदान मे मौजूद सबटा पुलिस अधिकारी कए सतर्क रखने छी आ सार्वजनिक संपत्ति क सुरक्षा आ कम स कम बल प्रयोग स कोनो तरह क परस्पर विरोधी स्थिति कए रोकबाक कोशिश मे छी।

title: Electric fence turning into death trap - The Rising Nepal
description: Electric fence turning into death trap  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
By Our Correspondent, Damak, July 31: An electric fence installed to protect crops from elephants has once again turned into a death trap in Mayalu Forest in Bhadrapur Municipality-4, Jhapa.

Illegal electric wires installed to protect farmland from elephant raids are increasingly posing a serious threat to human life.

At around 9:00 am on Wednesday, 65-year-old Jyoti Limbu was electrocuted after coming into contact with an exposed electric wire installed around her field to drive away elephants in the Mayalu Forest area of Bhadrapur-4.

Her daughter-in-law, Sabita Khadka, later found her lying unconscious on the ground and informed the police, according to authorities.

Ranjan Awal, spokesperson for the District Police Office, Jhapa, said an investigation into the incident had begun. He said preliminary findings indicated that Limbu died after stepping on an electrified wire installed to protect crops from elephants.

Jhapa is the district worst affected by human-elephant conflict in Nepal, with both people and wildlife losing their lives to elephant attacks every year.

In response, some farmers have been directly connecting household electricity to exposed wires to drive elephants away at night. Although such electric fencing is prohibited by law, it is still being used in rural areas.

Farmers, particularly in areas bordering India where elephants regularly enter Nepal, are forced to suffer significant annual losses.

After elephants destroy crops such as paddy, maize, bananas and sugarcane, some farmers resort to using electric wires in violation of the law, and a number of people have lost their lives after coming into contact with them.

Laws governing forest and wildlife conservation do not permit the use of fences carrying exposed electric current. Such practices are punishable because they put the lives of both people and wildlife at risk. Nevertheless, farmers in elephant-affected areas continue to resort to the measure in an attempt to protect their crops.

The area stretching from Bahundangi to Bhadrapur in Jhapa is regarded as one of Nepal’s worst-affected areas for human-elephant conflict. Herds of elephants entering from forests in India destroy crops, damage houses and sometimes cause human casualties every year, increasing fear among locals.

According to Arjun Karki, chairperson of Mechinagar Municipality Ward No. 4 and a wildlife conservationist, the number of human casualties is increasing as residents take risks by electrifying wires even around their homes to keep elephants away.

Elephants have been entering Nepal almost daily from India through Hattigauda in Bahundangi, according to locals.

More than 40 elephants have been entering Nepal, although they sometimes split into smaller groups in search of food.

Elephant researcher Shankar Luitel said more than four dozen elephants were currently roaming at different local levels in Jhapa in search of food.

हमर संवाददाता, दमक, 31 जुलाई : झापा के भद्रपुर नगरपालिका-4 के मायालू वन मे हाथी सं फसल के बचाबय लेल लगाओल गेल बिजली के बाड़ एक बेर फेर सं मौत के जाल मे बदलि गेल अछि.

खेती के जमीन के हाथी के छापा सं बचाबय लेल लगाओल गेल अवैध बिजली के तार मानव जीवन के लेल तेजी सं गंभीर खतरा पैदा क रहल अछि.

बुधदिन भोर करीब 9:00 बजे भद्रपुर-4 के मायालू वन क्षेत्र मे हाथी के भगाबय लेल अपन खेत के चारू कात लगाओल गेल उजागर बिजली के तार के संपर्क मे आबि 65 वर्षीय ज्योति लिम्बू के करंट लागि गेल छल.

बाद मे हुनकर पुतोहु सबिता खड्का हुनका जमीन पर बेहोश पड़ल पाबि पुलिस के सूचना देलक, अधिकारी के अनुसार।

जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय झापाके प्रवक्ता रंजन अवल घटनाके अनुसन्धान शुरु भेल जानकारी देलनि । ओ कहलनि जे, प्रारंभिक निष्कर्ष सं पता चलैत अछि जे हाथी सं फसल के बचाबय लेल लगाओल गेल विद्युतीकृत तार पर कदम रखला के बाद लिम्बू के मौत भ गेल छल.

झापा नेपालमे मानव-हाथीक द्वन्द्वसँ सबसँ बेसी प्रभावित जिला अछि, जाहिमे हरेक वर्ष हाथीक आक्रमणसँ लोक आ वन्यजीव दुनूक जान चलि जाइत अछि ।

एकरऽ जवाब म॑ कुछ किसान सीधा घरऽ के बिजली क॑ उजागर तार स॑ जोड़तें हुअ॑ रात म॑ हाथी क॑ भगाबै के काम करी रहलऽ छै । हालांकि एहि तरहक इलेक्ट्रिक फेंसिंग कानून मे मना अछि, मुदा ग्रामीण क्षेत्र मे एखनो एकर उपयोग भ रहल अछि।

खास क भारतक सीमावर्ती इलाका मे जतय हाथी नियमित रूप सँ नेपाल मे प्रवेश करैत अछि ओतय किसान लोकनि केँ सालाना काफी नुकसान होबय पड़ैत छनि ।

हाथी के धान, मक्का, केरा, गन्ना जैसन फसल के नष्ट करला के बाद कुछ किसान कानून के उल्लंघन करतें हुअय बिजली के तार के इस्तेमाल के सहारा लेत॑ छै, आरू ओकरा संपर्क म॑ ऐला के बाद कईएक लोगऽ के जान चली गेलऽ छै ।

वन आ वन्यजीव संरक्षण कें नियंत्रित करय वाला कानून उजागर बिजली धारा कें ले जाय वाला बाड़ कें उपयोग कें अनुमति नहि देयत छै. एहन प्रथा दंडनीय अछि कियाक त एहि स लोक आ वन्यजीव दुनू क जान खतरा मे पड़ैत अछि। एकरऽ बावजूद हाथी प्रभावित क्षेत्रऽ के किसान अपनऽ फसल के सुरक्षा के कोशिश म॑ ई उपाय के सहारा लेत॑ रहै छै ।

झापा केरऽ बहुंडंगी स॑ ल॑ क॑ भद्रपुर तलक फैललऽ ई क्षेत्र क॑ नेपाल केरऽ मानव-हाथी संघर्ष केरऽ सबसें बेसी प्रभावित क्षेत्रऽ म॑ स॑ एक मानलऽ जाय छै । भारत मे जंगल सं प्रवेश करय वाला हाथी के झुंड हर साल फसल के नष्ट करैत अछि, घर के नुकसान पहुंचाबैत अछि आओर कखनो काल मानव के नुकसान सेहो पहुंचबैत अछि, जाहि सं स्थानीय लोक मे डर बढ़ैत अछि.

मेचिनगर नगरपालिका वार्ड नम्बर ४ के अध्यक्ष आ वन्यजीव संरक्षणकर्मी अर्जुन कार्की के अनुसार हाथी के दूर राखय लेल घर के आसपास तक तार के विद्युतीकरण क निवासी सब जोखिम उठाबय के कारण मानव हताहत के संख्या बढ़ि रहल अछि।

बहुदंगी के हट्टीगौड़ा के माध्यम स भारत स लगभग रोज हाथी नेपाल में प्रवेश करैत आबि रहल अछि स्थानीय लोक के अनुसार।

४० सँ बेसी हाथी नेपाल मे प्रवेश करैत आबि रहल अछि, यद्यपि ओ कखनो काल भोजनक खोज मे छोट-छोट समूह मे बँटि जाइत अछि ।

हाथी शोधकर्ता शंकर लुइटेल कहलनि जे, एखन झापा मे चारि दर्जन सं बेसी हाथी भोजन के तलाश मे अलग-अलग स्थानीय स्तर पर घुमि रहल अछि।

title: Nepal Police Urges Calm Amidst Religious and Social Tensions - Ratopati
description: Nepal Police Urges Calm Amidst Religious and Social Tensions  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. Nepal Police has expressed concern over the recent activities of religious and social tensions seen in various parts of the country and has made a special appeal to all citizens to maintain restraint and mutual harmony.

Inspector General of Police (IGP) Dan Bahadur Karki, through a video message, stated that the main identity of Nepali society is 'unity in diversity' and it is everyone's shared responsibility to preserve it.

Karki clarified that activities that disturb religious harmony and create an atmosphere of fear and terror have been observed in some places, especially in the eastern Terai, and such actions will not benefit anyone. He concluded that spreading rumors through social media, making provocative statements, and violating the law will only increase tension, mistrust, and division in society.

In the video message, Karki said, "Our religions, traditions, and cultures may be different, but the country is one and our feelings are also one." He urged everyone to adopt the path of wisdom, restraint, and harmony instead of spreading rumors and hatred during this sensitive time. The message mentioned that respecting the rights, beliefs, and dignity of others is the main need of the hour.

Nepal Police has appealed to all Nepali brothers and sisters to respect each other's culture and beliefs with mutual respect and tolerance. Furthermore, the police have requested all citizens to cooperate in strengthening national unity and brotherhood and maintaining social peace.

पुलिस महानिरीक्षक दान बहादुर कार्की वीडियो संदेश के माध्यम स नेपाली समाज के मुख्य पहिचान ‘विविधता मे एकता’ अछि आ एकरा संरक्षित करब सबहक साझी जिम्मेदारी रहल बतौलनि।

कार्की न॑ स्पष्ट करलकै कि धार्मिक सौहार्द क॑ भंग करै वाला आरू भय आरू आतंक के माहौल पैदा करै वाला गतिविधि कुछ जगह खास करी क॑ पूर्वी तराई म॑ देखलऽ गेलऽ छै आरू ऐसनऽ काम स॑ ककरो कोनो फायदा नै होतै । हुनी निष्कर्ष निकाललकै कि सोशल मीडिया के माध्यम स॑ अफवाह फैलाबै, भड़काऊ बयान देना, आरू कानून के उल्लंघन स॑ समाज म॑ तनाव, अविश्वास, आरू विभाजन ही बढ़तै ।

वीडियो संदेश म॑ कार्की न॑ कहलकै कि हमरऽ धर्म, परंपरा, आरू संस्कृति अलग-अलग होय सकै छै, लेकिन देश एक छै आरू हमरऽ भावना भी एक छै । ओ सब गोटे स आग्रह केलथि जे एहि संवेदनशील समय मे अफवाह आ घृणा पसारबाक बदला बुद्धि, संयम, आ सौहार्द के मार्ग अपनाबी। संदेश में उल्लेख करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै कि दोसरऽ के अधिकार, मान्यता, आरू गरिमा के सम्मान करना घड़ी के मुख्य जरूरत छै ।

नेपाल प्रहरी समस्त नेपाली भाई-बहिन सँ आपसी सम्मान आ सहिष्णुता के साथ एक दोसर के संस्कृति आ विश्वास के सम्मान करबाक अपील केने अछि । संगहि पुलिस सब नागरिक स आग्रह केलक अछि जे राष्ट्रीय एकता आ भाईचारा कए मजबूत करबा मे आ सामाजिक शांति कायम रखबा मे सहयोग करी।

title: Nims Purja, 5 Nepalis missing on Broad Peak - Nepali Times
description: Nims Purja, 5 Nepalis missing on Broad Peak  Nepali Times
publisher.title: Nepali Times
full_article:
Noted Nepali-British mountaineer Nirmal (Nims) Purja is among ten climbers that was struck by a massive avalanche on Broad Peak in the Karakoram range of Pakistan on Thursday morning.

The team was making its way from Camp 2 to Camp 3 when the avalanche hit them at an elevation of 6,600m. Since everyone was swept away, staff at Base Camp found out about the avalanche only 12 hours later.

The Pakistan Air Force deployed search and rescue helicopters at first light on Friday. GPS tracking on some of the climbers in the group reportedly shows them drop hundreds of meters below the climbing route, a possible indication that they were hit by the avalanche.

Purja, 5 Nepali guides and a Pakistani were from four expeditions taking international clients from the US, Oman and China to the summit of the 8,047m peak.

Nims Purja, 43, a former Royal Navy Special Boat Service commando, shattered the world record for climbing all the world’s 14 highest mountains in just 6 months and six days in 2019 — a feat that had taken seven years by a previous Korean climber.

Purja was also featured in the documentary 14 Peaks: Nothing is Impossible about his humble beginnings in Nepal, his commando life in the British military and his ambition-driven mountaineering career. The film shows him risking his life saving other climbers on Kangchenjunga, and nearly being killed in a fall on Annapurna.

His other feats include leading a team of nine Nepali climbers for the first-ever winter ascent of K2, the world’s second-highest mountain in Pakistan, in 2021. Last year he was the first climber to summit Everest, Lhotse and Makalu — all within 48 hours.

After allegations that he had not climbed the true summit of Manaslu in 2019 and that he had used oxygen in many of his climbs, Purja appeared to be chasing another record: climbing all 14 eight-thousand-metre peaks twice without oxygen. Purja was also accused by two women clients of sexual harrassment, in which he denied any wrongdoing.

Broad Peak would have been the second last peak to complete the feat, and he reportedly decided to climb it while on another expedition in the Karakoram this month.

Nims Purja heads the company Elite Exped which organises commercial expeditions for clients on Himalayan peaks. Purja had come to Pakistan after completing the Spring 2026 climbing season on Mt Everest for expeditions on both the north and south sides of the mountain.

Till press time on Saturday morning in Pakistan, rescue teams had not yet located the climbers below Broad Peak.

पाकिस्तान केरऽ काराकोरम श्रृंखला केरऽ ब्रॉड पीक प॑ गुरुवार क॑ भोर म॑ भारी हिमस्खलन स॑ टकराबै वाला दस पर्वतारोही म॑ स॑ प्रसिद्ध नेपाली-ब्रिटिश पर्वतारोही निर्मल (निम्स) पुरजा भी शामिल छै ।

टीम कैंप 2 स कैंप 3 के रास्ता बना रहल छल कि हिमस्खलन 6600 मीटर के ऊंचाई पर आबि गेल। चूँकि सब कियो बहरा गेल छल, बेस कैंप के कर्मचारी के हिमस्खलन के बारे मे मात्र 12 घंटा बाद पता चलल.

पाकिस्तान वायुसेना शुक्रदिन पहिल रोशनी मे खोज आ बचाव हेलीकॉप्टर तैनात केलक अछि। खबर छै कि समूह केरऽ कुछ पर्वतारोही प॑ जीपीएस ट्रैकिंग स॑ पता चलै छै कि वू पर्वतारोही मार्ग स॑ सैकड़ों मीटर नीचे गिरी जाय छै, जे संभावित संकेत छै कि ओकरा हिमस्खलन स॑ टकराबै के छै ।

पुरजा, ५ नेपाली गाइड आरू एक पाकिस्तानी अमेरिका, ओमान आरू चीन केरऽ अंतरराष्ट्रीय ग्राहकऽ क॑ ८,०४७ मीटर केरऽ चोटी प॑ पहुँचै वाला चार अभियान स॑ छेलै ।

43 वर्षीय निम्स पुर्जा, जे रॉयल नेवी स्पेशल बोट सर्विस केरऽ कमांडो छेलै, न॑ 2019 म॑ महज 6 महीना आरू छह दिन म॑ दुनिया केरऽ सब 14 सबसें ऊँचऽ पहाड़ प॑ चढ़ै के विश्व रिकॉर्ड क॑ तोड़ी देलकै — जेकरा म॑ कोरियाई पर्वतारोही क॑ सात साल लगलै ।

पुरजा क॑ नेपाल म॑ हुनकऽ विनम्र शुरुआत, ब्रिटिश सेना म॑ हुनकऽ कमांडो जीवन आरू महत्वाकांक्षा स॑ संचालित पर्वतारोहण कैरियर के बारे म॑ डॉक्यूमेंट्री १४ पीक्स: नोथिंग इज इम्पॉसिबल म॑ भी पेश करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै । फिल्म म॑ ओकरा कांगचेनजंगा प॑ दोसरऽ पर्वतारोही सिनी क॑ बचाबै लेली अपनऽ जान जोखिम म॑ डालै के काम करलऽ गेलऽ छै, आरू अन्नपूर्णा प॑ गिरला स॑ लगभग मौत होय गेलऽ छै ।

हुनकऽ अन्य कारनामा म॑ २०२१ म॑ पाकिस्तान केरऽ दुनिया केरऽ दोसरऽ सबसें ऊँचऽ पहाड़ के२ प॑ पहिलऽ बार शीतकालीन चढ़ाई लेली नौ नेपाली पर्वतारोही के टीम के नेतृत्व करना शामिल छै ।पिछला साल हुनी एवरेस्ट, ल्होत्से आरू मकालू केरऽ शिखर प॑ पहुँचै वाला पहिलऽ पर्वतारोही छेलै — ई सब ४८ घंटा के भीतर ।

2019 म॑ मनसलू केरऽ असली शिखर प॑ नै चढ़ै के आरोप के बाद आरू अपनऽ बहुत चढ़ाई म॑ ऑक्सीजन के इस्तेमाल करै के आरोप के बाद पुरजा एगो आरू रिकॉर्ड के पीछा करतें नजर ऐलै कि बिना ऑक्सीजन के दू बार सब 14 आठ हजार मीटर के चोटी प॑ चढ़ना । पुरजा पर दू टा महिला मुवक्किल के तरफ सं यौन उत्पीड़न के आरोप सेहो लागल छल, जाहि मे ओ कोनो गलत काज सं इनकार केलनि.

ब्रॉड पीक ई करतब पूरा करै वाला दोसरऽ आखिरी चोटी होतै, आरू खबर छै कि हुनी ई महीना काराकोरम म॑ एगो आरू अभियान के दौरान एकरा प॑ चढ़ै के फैसला करलकै ।

निम्स पुरजा कंपनी एलिट एक्सपेड के प्रमुख छै जे हिमालयी चोटी पर ग्राहकऽ लेली व्यावसायिक अभियान के आयोजन करै छै । पुरजा पहाड़ केरऽ उत्तर आरू दक्षिण दोनों तरफ केरऽ अभियान लेली माउंट एवरेस्ट प॑ वसंत २०२६ केरऽ चढ़ाई के मौसम पूरा करी क॑ पाकिस्तान आबी गेलऽ छेलै ।

पाकिस्तान म॑ शनिदिन सुबह प्रेस टाइम तलक बचाव टीम न॑ अभी तलक ब्रॉड पीक स॑ नीचें पर्वतारोही के पता नै लगाय सकलऽ छेलै ।

title: Nims Purja among 10 climbers missing after Broad Peak avalanche in Pakistan - The Himalayan Times
description: Nims Purja among 10 climbers missing after Broad Peak avalanche in Pakistan  The Himalayan Times
publisher.title: The Himalayan Times
full_article:
KATHMANDU, JULY 31

At least 10 climbers, including renowned Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja "Nimsdai", have gone missing after a massive avalanche struck the climbing route on Pakistan's 8,047-metre Broad Peak since Thursday, expedition officials said.

According to the Alpine Club of Pakistan, the missing include three climbers from Seven Summit Treks, three from Elite Exped, two from Imagine Nepal Treks, and two Pakistani high-altitude guides.

Search-and-rescue efforts are under way, with helicopters being mobilised to locate the missing climbers. Those still out of contact include Purja; a Russian-American climber and a Sherpa from Elite Exped; an Omani climber accompanied by two Sherpas from SST; a Chinese climber with a Sherpa from Imagine Nepal Treks; and two Pakistani guides.

title: Nepal’s PM urges calm after unrest leaves 3 dead - Free Malaysia Today
description: Nepal’s PM urges calm after unrest leaves 3 dead  Free Malaysia Today
publisher.title: Free Malaysia Today
full_article:
Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah called for the public ‘to exercise patience and restrain and maintain peace, harmony, brotherhood and national unity’. (EPA Images pic)

KATHMANDU : Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Thursday appealed for calm after clashes between Hindu and Muslim groups in the country’s south sparked unrest that has left three people dead.

Shah, who has kept a low profile since being elected in March, broke his silence to deliver his first address to the nation, calling on his countrymen to be “responsible citizens and remove the clouds of unrest”.

The violence began late Sunday in a village in the southern Sunsari district, which borders India, after an argument over loud music and the use of religious flags during a Hindu procession, according to officials.

Police opened fire to disperse the crowd, said local official Poshan Lamichhane. Two men died in the unrest, according to police spokesman Abi Narayan Kafle.

Authorities are investigating the deaths and have imposed a curfew in Sunsari and neighbouring districts to prevent further clashes.

A third man was killed Thursday in the nearby Siraha district during a demonstration that took place while the curfew was in force.

“I, on behalf of the government, sincerely appeal to the citizens, civil society, religious communities, all respected leaders, all political parties and responsible media, to exercise patience and restrain and maintain peace, harmony, brotherhood and national unity,” Shah said in a video address.

Nepal, a secular republic where more than 80%of the population is Hindu, has seen tensions flare occasionally in the southern plains, where sizeable Hindu and Muslim communities live side by side.

In his address, Shah vowed that the investigation would be “completely fair and transparent”.

“The government is committed to bringing to justice whoever is responsible for the incident,” he said.

Kafle, the police official, said efforts were being made to restore order.

“We have kept all police officials in the field on alert and are trying to protect public property and prevent any conflicting situation with minimal use of force,” he told AFP.

title: 10 climbers led by a renowned Nepalese mountaineer are missing on a Pakistan peak - KSAT
description: 10 climbers led by a renowned Nepalese mountaineer are missing on a Pakistan peak  KSAT
publisher.title: KSAT
full_article:
ISLAMABAD – Ten international climbers led by a renowned Nepal-born mountaineer were missing after an avalanche struck Broad Peak, one of the world’s highest mountains in northern Pakistan.

The Alpine Club of Pakistan received initial reports that the avalanche struck the team led by Nirmal Purja and the climbers have been out of communication since then, club Vice President Karrar Haidri said in a statement late Thursday.

Recommended Videos

The expedition includes five Nepalese climbers, Pakistani mountaineer Sohail Sakhi of Hunza, Omani climber Nathira, American climber Mallory Geis, a Chinese climber identified as Wang, and another foreign climber, Haidri said.

The club's president, Maj. Gen. Irfan Arshad, and its senior leaders were in contact with government officials to facilitate an immediate search-and-rescue operation.

The club said every effort was being made to mobilize helicopters and other rescue resources quickly, subject to weather and operational conditions.

Nirmal Purja, whom the club identified by a second name, Nims Dai, is a Nepal-born British citizen who scaled the world's 14 highest peaks in 189 days in 2019, holding a record for the fastest climb until a Norwegian woman and her Nepali Sherpa guide set a new record in 2023. Purja’s climbs were made into a popular Netflix documentary, “14 Peaks: Nothing is Impossible.”

The 8,047-meter (26,401-foot) Broad Peak in the Karakoram range is the world's 12th highest mountain. Pakistan is home to several top mountain peaks and climbers flock from all over the world to attempt to scale the summits.

“The Alpine Club of Pakistan is closely monitoring the situation and coordinating with all concerned stakeholders,” the statement said. It added that the club stands in solidarity with the climbers’ families and the international mountaineering community.

क्लब केरऽ उपाध्यक्ष कररर हैदरी न॑ गुरुवार देर रात जारी बयान म॑ कहलकै कि पाकिस्तान केरऽ अल्पाइन क्लब क॑ प्रारंभिक खबर मिललै कि निर्मल पुरजा के नेतृत्व वाला टीम प॑ हिमस्खलन आबी गेलऽ छै आरू तहिया स॑ पर्वतारोही सिनी के बीच संवाद बंद होय गेलऽ छै ।

हैदरी कहलनि जे, एहि अभियान मे पांच नेपाली पर्वतारोही, हुन्जा के पाकिस्तानी पर्वतारोही सोहेल सखी, ओमानी पर्वतारोही नाथिरा, अमेरिकी पर्वतारोही मैलोरी गेस, चीनी पर्वतारोही मैलोरी गेस, जेकर पहचान वांग के रूप मे भेल अछि, आ एकटा आओर विदेशी पर्वतारोही शामिल छथि।

क्लब न॑ कहलकै कि मौसम आरू परिचालन केरऽ स्थिति के आधार प॑ हेलीकॉप्टर आरू अन्य बचाव संसाधन क॑ जल्दी स॑ जुटाबै के हर संभव प्रयास करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै ।

निर्मल पुरजा, जिनकर पहचान क्लब दोसर नाम निम्स दाई स केने अछि, नेपाल में जन्मल ब्रिटिश नागरिक छथि जे 2019 में 189 दिन में दुनिया के 14 सबस ऊँच चोटी के स्केल केने छलाह, जखन तक कि एकटा नार्वे के महिला आ हुनकर नेपाली शेर्पा गाइड 2023 में एकटा नव रिकॉर्ड नै बनौने छल, सबस तेज चढ़ाई के रिकॉर्ड बनौने छल।पुरजा के चढ़ाई के एकटा लोकप्रिय नेटफ्लिक्स डॉक्यूमेंट्री, “14 चोटी : किछुओ असंभव नहि अछि।”

काराकोरम श्रृंखला केरऽ ८,०४७ मीटर (२६,४०१ फीट) केरऽ ब्रॉड पीक दुनिया केरऽ १२वां सबसें ऊंचऽ पहाड़ छेकै । पाकिस्तान म॑ कईएक शीर्ष पहाड़ी चोटी छै आरू ई शिखर प॑ चढ़ै के कोशिश करै लेली दुनिया भर स॑ पर्वतारोही के भीड़ लगै छै ।

बयान मँ कहलौ गेलौ छै कि पाकिस्तान केरौ अल्पाइन क्लब स्थिति प बारीकी स॑ नजर रखी रहलऽ छै आरू सब संबंधित हितधारकऽ के साथ समन्वय करी रहलऽ छै । एकरा म॑ आरू कहलऽ गेलऽ छै कि ई क्लब पर्वतारोही केरऽ परिवार आरू अंतर्राष्ट्रीय पर्वतारोहण समुदाय के साथ एकजुटता म॑ खड़ा छै ।

title: Police Arrest 25 in Drug Raids Across Nepal - Ratopati
description: Police Arrest 25 in Drug Raids Across Nepal  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. A police team on regular patrol has arrested 25 people with drugs from various parts of the country.

According to the Central Police News Room, they were arrested with various types of drugs from Teku and Tinathana Gairigaun in Kathmandu, Biratnagar Airport and Haruchok in Morang, Chanoute in Surkhet, Chepang Bazaar, Danfe, Lalpur Chowk and Kothiyaghat in Bardiya, Milan Chowk in Kailali, Chandani Chowk in Jhapa, Jurouni in Dang and Syaule in Dadeldhura.

According to the police, two people were arrested from Teku with 12 grams of brown heroin-like substance, four people from Tinathana Gairigaun with 30 tablets of Tramadol, one person from Biratnagar Airport with 18 grams 48 milligrams of brown heroin-like substance, and two people from Haruchok with 650 milligrams of brown heroin-like substance.

Similarly, one person was arrested from Chanoute with 5 grams 690 milligrams of brown heroin-like substance, eight people from Chepang Bazaar, Danfe, Lalpur Chowk and Kothiyaghat-Oralibazaar with various quantities of brown heroin-like substance, two people from Milan Chowk with 240 milligrams of brown heroin-like substance, and one person from Chandani Chowk with 1 gram 250 milligrams of brown heroin-like substance and cash Rs 12,225.

Similarly, one person was arrested from Jurouni in Dang with 35 kilograms of hashish and three people from Syaule with 160 milligrams of brown heroin-like substance.

title: 10 climbers, including Nepal's Nirmal Purja, feared missing after avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak - Firstpost
description: 10 climbers, including Nepal's Nirmal Purja, feared missing after avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak  Firstpost
publisher.title: Firstpost
full_article:
A 10-member international mountaineering team led by famous Nepal-born former Royal Marine Nirmal Purja is feared missing after an avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak, the world’s highest mountain. Pakistani mountaineering officials said that the avalanche took place on Thursday.

The avalanche hit the 8,047-metre (26,400 ft) peak in the Karakoram range. The authorities noted that as of now, there has been no subsequent communication with the team, the BBC reported. An American, a Chinese national, an Omani and five Nepalis are said to be part of the climbing group.

STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD

It is pertinent to note that Purja, the expedition leader, is known for climbing all 14 of the world’s 8,000-metre-plus mountains in just over six months in 2019. “We are coordinating with the authorities and trying to arrange a helicopter rescue on Friday morning Pakistani time, depending on weather conditions,” Karrar Haidri, the vice-president of the Alpine Club of Pakistan, told the BBC.

More from World Mount Everest could soon become harder to climb: Nepal’s new rules explained Globe at a glance: From Saudi's Red Sea naval coalition to chaos at Spain-Morocco border

The challenging mountain peak

Broad Peak in Pakistan is regarded as one of the more challenging mountains for expeditions, and is ranked as the world’s 12th highest peak. In a separate statement, the Alpine Club of Pakistan said it had been “in constant contact” with the authorities to ensure that “all available resources are mobilised at the earliest opportunity”.

“The Club prays for the safety and successful rescue of all the climbers and stands in solidarity with their families and the international mountaineering community during this difficult time,” it added.

According to the BBC, Pujra joined the British Army in 2003 and became a Royal Marine in 2009. His climbing career began when he walked to Everest Base Camp back in 2012 and, instead of returning as planned, decided to climb the entire mountain.

हिमस्खलन काराकोरम श्रृंखला केरऽ ८,०४७ मीटर (२६,४०० फीट) के चोटी प॑ पहुँचलै । बीबीसी केरऽ रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक अधिकारियऽ न॑ नोट करलकै कि अभी तलक टीम के साथ बाद म॑ कोय संवाद नै होय सकलऽ छै । एक अमेरिकी, एक चीनी नागरिक, एक ओमानी आ पाँच नेपाली पर्वतारोही समूह के हिस्सा बताओल जा रहल अछि ।

चुनौतीपूर्ण पहाड़ी चोटी

ओकरा मँ आरू कहलौ गेलौ छै कि क्लब सब पर्वतारोही के सुरक्षा आरू सफल बचाव के प्रार्थना करै छै आरू ई कठिन समय मँ हुनकौ परिवार आरू अंतरराष्ट्रीय पर्वतारोहण समुदाय के साथ एकजुटता के साथ खड़ा छै ।

title: 10 climbers, led by Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja missing after avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak - theweek.in
description: 10 climbers, led by Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja missing after avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak  theweek.in
publisher.title: theweek.in
full_article:
A group of 10 international climbers led by a Nepali mountaineer, Nirmal Purja, is feared missing after an avalanche struck the team late Thursday at the Broad Peak, one of the highest mountains in northern Pakistan.

The vice president of the Alpine Club of Pakistan, Karrar Haidiri, said that the climbers have been out of communication since then.

The expedition included five Nepalese climbers, Nepal-born British mountaineer Nirmal Purja, Pakistani mountaineer Sohail Sakhi of Hunzqa, Omani climber Nathira, American climber Mallory Geis and a Chinese climber Wang. The group also included an unidentified foreign climber, according to Haidiri.

The Pakistan Alpine Club said that the avalanche struck the 8,047-meter-high Broad Peak in the Karakoram Range around noon Thursday.

The accident occurred when the team was on an expedition to the peak.

The Alpine club has found that the tracking device Nirmal Purja carried showed movement, raising hopes for the rescue teams.

The device’s location has changed after the avalanche, according to Purja’s business partner and Nepal MP Mingma Gyaby Sherpa.

“Every possible effort is being made to ensure that helicopter support and all available rescue resources are mobilised at the earliest opportunity, subject to weather and operational conditions,” the club said.

"We are coordinating with the authorities and trying to arrange a helicopter rescue on Friday morning Pakistani time, depending on weather conditions," Haidri told the BBC.

Purja, 43, also known as Nims Dai, has broken multiple climbing records since he became a full-time mountaineer and tour guide in 2018 after leaving the British Military.

He climbed all 14 “eight-thousanders”, peaks above 8,000 metres, or 26,000 feet, in six months and six days between April and October 2019, breaking a record that year.

Purja was also part of a team of nine other Nepalese climbers who completed the first winter ascent of K2 in 2021.

Purja had also previously joined the British Army in 2003 and became a Royal Marine in 2009.

पाकिस्तान केरऽ अल्पाइन क्लब केरऽ उपाध्यक्ष कररर हैदिरी न॑ कहलकै कि तहिया स॑ पर्वतारोही सिनी के संपर्क स॑ बाहर छै ।

एहि अभियान मे पाँच नेपाली पर्वतारोही, नेपाल मे जन्मल ब्रिटिश पर्वतारोही निर्मल पुर्जा, हुन्जका के पाकिस्तानी पर्वतारोही सोहेल सखी, ओमानी पर्वतारोही नाथिरा, अमेरिकी पर्वतारोही मैलोरी गेस आ एकटा चीनी पर्वतारोही वांग शामिल छल । हैदिरी के अनुसार समूह में एकटा अज्ञात विदेशी पर्वतारोही सेहो शामिल छल।

पुरजा केरऽ बिजनेस पार्टनर आरू नेपाल केरऽ सांसद मिंगमा ग्याबी शेर्पा के अनुसार हिमस्खलन के बाद डिवाइस केरऽ स्थान बदली गेलऽ छै ।

क्लब नँ कहलकै, “हर संभव प्रयास करलौ जाय रहलौ छै कि हेलीकॉप्टर सपोर्ट आरू सब उपलब्ध बचाव संसाधन क ​​मौसम आरू परिचालन के स्थिति के आधार प जल्दी स॑ जल्दी मौका प॑ जुटान करलऽ जाय ।

हैदरी न॑ बीबीसी क॑ बतैलकै कि हम्में अधिकारियऽ के साथ समन्वय करी रहलऽ छियै आरू मौसम के हिसाब स॑ शुक्रवार के सुबह पाकिस्तानी समय प॑ हेलीकॉप्टर स॑ बचाव के व्यवस्था करै के कोशिश करी रहलऽ छियै ।

43 वर्षीय पुर्जा, जेकरा निम्स दाई के नाम स॑ भी जानलऽ जाय छै, न॑ ब्रिटिश मिलिट्री छोड़ला के बाद २०१८ म॑ पूर्णकालिक पर्वतारोही आरू टूर गाइड बनला के बाद स॑ कईएक पर्वतारोही रिकॉर्ड तोड़ी चुकलऽ छै ।

अप्रैल आरू अक्टूबर २०१९ के बीच छह महीना आरू छह दिन म॑ हुनी सब १४ “आठ-हजार”, ८,००० मीटर यानी २६,००० फीट स॑ ऊपर के चोटी प॑ चढ़ी क॑ वू साल एगो रिकॉर्ड तोड़ी देलकै ।

पुरजा 2021 मे के2 के पहिल शीतकालीन आरोहण पूरा करय वाला नौ अन्य नेपाली पर्वतारोही के टीम के हिस्सा सेहो छल.

title: Pakistan rescuers find 4 bodies of the 10 climbers missing on Broad Peak after an avalanche - The New Indian Express
description: Pakistan rescuers find 4 bodies of the 10 climbers missing on Broad Peak after an avalanche  The New Indian Express
publisher.title: The New Indian Express
full_article:
ISLAMABAD: Rescuers searching for 10 climbers missing after an avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak located four bodies Friday and were continuing to search for the other six, officials said.

Efforts were underway to retrieve the bodies of the four climbers despite the harsh weather, according to the senior government officials. The officials, who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media, did not immediately identify whose bodies were found.

“The team has been out of communication since Thursday,” said Karrar Haidri, vice president of the Alpine Club of Pakistan, who said army helicopters had joined the search-and-rescue operation and authorities were in contact with the families of the missing climbers.

According to the Alpine Club, the expedition included five Nepali climbers, Pakistani mountaineer Sohail Sakhi from Hunza, Omani climber Nathira, American climber Mallory Geis, a Chinese climber identified only as Wang, and another foreign climber.

The expedition leader was the renowned moutaineer Nirmal Purja, a Nepal-born former soldier in the British army widely known as Nims Dai. He climbed the world’s 14 highest peaks in a record 189 days in 2019, an achievement featured in the Netflix documentary, “14 Peaks: Nothing is Impossible.” His record was surpassed in 2023.

Moving Mountains, a travel company based in Pakistan, announced late last month that the expedition team was on its way to the small town of Askole and wished them a safe journey climbing Broad Peak. The company said this was Geis’ first try at an 8,000-meter peak in Pakistan, while it was expected to be Sakhi’s final one.

इस्लामाबाद : पाकिस्तान केरऽ ब्रॉड पीक प॑ हिमस्खलन के बाद लापता १० पर्वतारोही के खोज करै वाला बचावकर्मी न॑ शुक्रवार क॑ चार शव के पता लगैलकै आरू बाकी छह के खोज जारी रखलकै ।

सरकारक वरिष्ठ अधिकारीक अनुसार कठोर मौसमक बादो चारिटा पर्वतारोहीक लाश बरामद करबाक प्रयास चलि रहल छल। मीडिया सं बात करय के अधिकार नहिं रहला के कारण नाम नहिं बताबय के शर्त पर बात करय वाला अधिकारी तत्काल पहचान नहिं केलनि जे केकर लाश भेटल अछि.

पाकिस्तान केरऽ अल्पाइन क्लब केरऽ उपाध्यक्ष कररर हैदरी न॑ कहलकै कि गुरुवार स॑ टीम केरऽ संवाद बंद छै, जेकरा म॑ सेना केरऽ हेलीकॉप्टर खोज-बचाव अभियान म॑ शामिल होय गेलऽ छै आरू अधिकारियऽ के संपर्क म॑ लापता पर्वतारोही के परिवार के संपर्क छै ।

अल्पाइन क्लब के अनुसार ई अभियान में पांच नेपाली पर्वतारोही, हुन्जा के पाकिस्तानी पर्वतारोही सोहेल सखी, ओमानी पर्वतारोही नाथिरा, अमेरिकी पर्वतारोही मैलोरी गेइस, चीनी पर्वतारोही मैलोरी गेस, जेकरऽ पहचान केवल वांग के नाम स॑ करलऽ गेलऽ छै, आरू एगो आरू विदेशी पर्वतारोही शामिल छेलै ।

अभियान केरऽ नेता छेलै प्रसिद्ध माउंटेनर निर्मल पुरजा, जे नेपाल म॑ जन्मलऽ ब्रिटिश सेना केरऽ पूर्व सैनिक छेलै जेकरा व्यापक रूप स॑ निम्स दाई के नाम स॑ जानलऽ जाय छै । 2019 म॑ रिकॉर्ड 189 दिन म॑ दुनिया केरऽ 14 सबसें उच्च चोटी प॑ चढ़ी गेलऽ छेलै, जेकरा नेटफ्लिक्स केरऽ डॉक्यूमेंट्री, “14 चोटी: नथिंग इज इम्पॉसिबल” म॑ पेश करलऽ गेलऽ उपलब्धि छै । हुनकर रिकॉर्ड 2023 मे पार भ गेल छल।

पाकिस्तान स्थित ट्रैवल कंपनी मूविंग माउंटेन न॑ पिछला महीना के अंत म॑ घोषणा करलकै कि अभियान टीम छोटऽ शहर अस्कोले के रास्ता प॑ छै आरू ओकरा ब्रॉड पीक प॑ चढ़ै के सुरक्षित यात्रा के कामना करलकै । कंपनी न॑ कहलकै कि पाकिस्तान म॑ ८,००० मीटर के चोटी प॑ गेइस केरऽ ई पहलऽ कोशिश छेकै, जबकि उम्मीद छै कि ई सखी केरऽ आखिरी कोशिश होतै ।

Previous deaths on Broad Peak published at 09:43 BST 09:43 BST Image source, AFP via Getty Images The first successful ascent of Broad Peak was in 1957, when a four-member Austrian expedition reached the summit. Since then, many more have climbed the 8,051m (26,414 ft) peak. And dozens have lost their lives to the mountain. 2013 marked one of Broad Peak's deadliest years, with at least six fatalities recorded. That March, two Polish climbers - aged 27 and 58 - were declared dead after they went missing during their descent from the summit. A few months later three Iranian climbers suffered a similar fate, and a German climber died after she slipped and was swept away by a mountain stream. One Chinese national is among the 10 climbers who lost contact after an avalanche on Thursday. The Chinese ministry has said it would provide help according to Pakistan's needs. BBC Nepali, Kathmandu Besides Nirmal Purja, there are a few other big names among the missing climbers, including Pur Bahadur Gurung - also known as Yukta - and Kili Pemba Sherpa. Yukta is certified by the International Federation of Mountain Guides Associations (IFMGA), and is very close to completing the 14 peaks challenge, where climbers attempt to summit the world's 14 mountains that rise at least 8,000m above sea level. Just last spring Yukta summited Nepal’s three "eight-thousanders", and by the end of that season had 10 Everest ascents and 12 eight-thousanders to his name. He was also part of the team that discovered a century-old shoe with the inscription "A.C. Irvine", believed to be of British climber Andrew "Sandy" Irvine, who vanished on Everest with George Mallory in 1924. Kili Pemba has so far summited Everest 15 times. In 2021 he was a member of a historic K2 winter expedition, alongwith several Nepali climbers including Nirmal Purja. Kili Pemba is also the guide who led double amputee Xia Boyu to summit Everest in 2018. Xia, a Chinese climber, had lost both legs decades earlier while attempting to reach Everest's summit. Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Climbers' GPS trackers provide clues published at 08:15 BST 08:15 BST As the search operation is under way, GPS data from the missing climbers' trackers provide clues on what happened when the avalanche hit Broad Peak. Samson Sharaf, the mentor of one of the 10 missing climbers, shared GPS data to industry website Climbing which indicate that the avalanche hit between 08:57 and 09:30 local time. At that time, American climber Mallory Geis, according to her GPS tracker, descended by 543m (1,781ft) while Omani climber Nadhira Al Harthy decended by 1,651m (5,417ft). Earlier, we reported that the tracking device belonging to Nirmal Purja had been showing movement. BBC Pakistan correspondent Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Broad Peak (in the background of this shot) is a notorious climbing route The search-and-rescue operation looking for 10 climbers missing in the Karakorum mountains has detected the location of four of their trackers - although they cannot identify if the climbers they belong to are dead or alive, according to the General Secretary of Pakistan’s Alpine club. The 10 climbers include renowned Nepal-born former British special forces soldier Nirmal Purja. All were climbing Broad Peak, the world’s 12th-highest mountain, when an avalanche struck. It is a nervous wait as rescuers try to reach the four climbers' location. Ayaz Shigri, general secretary of Pakistan Alpine Club, said that while the trackers had been located, there has been no movement from them. The rescue operation continues with drones and a ground team. Military helicopters are also on the way, and currently at the K2 base camp, according to Shigri. He estimated it to be a four-hour climb to reach the location of the four trackers with oxygen support. He hoped there would be more clarity by early evening, but said they did not know about the location of the other six climbers. Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Where is Broad Peak? published at 07:25 BST 07:25 BST Broad Peak is the twelfth tallest mountain on Earth and the third tallest in the Karakoram Range. Its name comes from its unusually long summit ridge, which extends for about 2 kilometers. There had been a total of 404 successful ascents of Broad Peak as of March 2012, while 21 climbers had died trying - a fatality rate of about 5 percent, said Nasa. Image source, Getty Images Image source, Getty Images Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Three trackers located, local officials say published at 07:15 BST 07:15 BST Local officials have told BBC Urdu that three trackers have been located at altitudes ranging from approximately 6,000m to 7,000m. Mountaineers usually carry GPS tracking devices when they climb major peaks. In 2024, the Nepali government made it mandatory for Mount Everest climbers to carry such trackers. BBC Nepali, Kathmandu Nepal’s Tourism Department has issued a statement saying it has instructed the country's embassy in Islamabad to coordinate with the Pakistan government in rescue efforts. Despite reports of multiple bodies having been found, the Department did not confirm any deaths - naming the six Nepalis from the expedition as "missing". Nepali companies based across several mountains in Pakistan are preparing to go to the scene and work with local authorities, it added. Department spokesperson Himal Gautam told the BBC: "There is a significant presence of Nepali Sherpas and expedition companies who are coordinating among themselves." "This is an unprecedented incident," Gautam added. "However, there are still some tiny hopes, with some conflicting information." Medhavi Gulati, a researcher on Sherpa and high-altitude mountaineering who is a lecturer at Panjab University says Nepal’s Sherpas are the most efficient highly-skilled staff when it comes to professional guiding. "Sherpas are highly preferred over local guides in because of their long history of high-altitude mountaineering and their professional training across diverse mountain environments." Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Pakistan’s mountains: the second major job market for Nepal’s Sherpas published at 06:38 BST 06:38 BST Pradeep Bashyal

BBC Nepali, Kathmandu Pakistan’s mountains have gained popularity as more and more people attempt to complete the 14 Peaks: the challenge of climbing all fourteen of the world's mountains that rise higher than 8,000 metres. Of these fourteen peaks, five are climbed from Pakistan, two from China (including Everest, which is also climbed from Nepal), and eight from Nepal. Nepal’s Sherpas, renowned for their mountain-guiding expertise, spend most of the spring climbing season working on Nepal’s high mountains. As the monsoon arrives in Nepal, many go to Pakistan for its climbing season before returning home for Nepal’s autumn expeditions. “The recently growing prestige of completing all 14 peaks has made Pakistan’s mountains the second major workplace for Nepal’s Sherpas,” says Khimlal Gautam, a Nepali mountaineer and author. “However, Sherpas are equally sought after across the world - from the mountains of Europe and the Americas, to Antarctica.” Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Four bodies found by rescue teams, says Alpine club president published at 06:29 BST 06:29 BST Breaking As many as four bodies have been recovered by ground rescue teams, president of the Alpine Club of Pakistan Irfan Arshad Khan has said in a post on Instagram. The BBC is unable to independently verify this. Earlier, we reported that Nepal's Ambassador to Pakistan, Rita Dhital, said she had acknowledged that there were reports of bodies found on the scene but said she had not received hat there was no official confirmation. Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Search under way for missing mountaineers published at 06:22 BST 06:22 BST The seach for the missing mountaineers on Broad Peak is under way, our teams on the ground in Pakistan can confirm. In an interview with Nepali news outlet Kantipur, Nepali Ambassador to Pakistan Rita Dhital says an aerial and ground search effort has been mobilised. Dhital says the aerial search involves helicopters and drones and acknowledged that there are unconfirmed reports of bodies found on the scene, but added that there was no official confirmation yet. Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 14 Peaks: Nirmal Purja's mountaineering record published at 06:08 BST 06:08 BST Image source, AFP via Getty Images Nirmal Purja, known as Nims Dai, holds multiple mountaineering records. But his most famous feat was set in 2019, when he climbed the world’s 14 tallest peaks in just six months - the shortest amount of time anyone has done that. The previous record for such a feat stood at nearly eight years. This journey, named Project Possible, was captured in the documentary 14 Peaks: Nothing is Impossible. As he approached the peak of Everest in May 2019, he snapped a photo of a snaking queue of climbers all waiting to summit The traffic jam photo went viral and sparked a conversation about dangerous overcrowding on the world’s tallest peak. The message he said he hoped to send with his ambitious mission was that anyone could achieve their dreams if they put their minds to it. "It's not about mountain climbing, it's about following your goals," he previously told the BBC. Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing What you need to know published at 05:53 BST 05:53 BST A group of mountaineers, including renowned Nepali-born climber Nirmal Purja are feared missing on Broad Peak, the world's 12th highest mountain. Here's what you need to know: The search will start as soon as the weather permits and the Pakistan Army has dispatched two helicopters

Purja is the leader of the expedition. He is famed for climbing all 14 of the world's 8,000-metre plus mountains in just over six months in 2019

The avalanche struck late on Thursday and the group has not been contacted since

Nepali media report two bodies have been found and have yet to be identified We'll bring you the latest updates as we get them - stay with us. BBC Nepali, Kathmandu Nepal's Mountaineering Association (NMA) is currently coordinating with the Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) in its rescue efforts, says Rajendra Bahadur Lama, General Secretary of NMA. "Some of our Sherpa friends based in K2 are going there for rescue efforts," he said, adding that there were reports that some mountaineers had been spotted from rescue helicopters, though this cannot be confirmed. The 10 climbers on the mountain are made up of guides and their foreign clients from three Nepali companies - Elite Exped, Seven Summit Treks and Imagine Nepal. Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Two bodies found after avalanche - report published at 05:21 BST 05:21 BST Nepali news outlet Kantipur is reporting now that two bodies of two climbers have been found at the scene. Thaneshwar Guragain, general manager of hiking agency Seven Summit Treks, told Kantipur that an identification process was underway. When asked about the possibility of finding other climbers alive, Guragain said their chanes were "slim", adding "the space for hope has become very narrow". BBC Pakistan correspondent It's just past 9am in Pakistan and two army rescue helicopters carrying rescue personnel and additional specialised equipment have been dispatched to support the ongoing search and rescue operation, the country's Alpine Club has told me. The helicopters are reinforcing efforts on the ground to assist the stranded climbers and enhance the effectiveness of the operation in the challenging high-altitude environment, they added. The Alpine Club also said they sincerely appreciated the prompt response and unwavering support of the Pakistan Army Aviation and all agencies involved and they remained hopeful for the safe recovery of the missing climbers and would continue to provide updates Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Climbers deployed from other mountains to help with search - Nepal lawmaker published at 04:47 BST 04:47 BST Koh Ewe

Live reporter Climbers on other mountains in the region have been deployed to help with search efforts on Broad Peak, a Nepalese lawmaker has just told the BBC. Climbers in K2 and K3, two nearby mountains in the Karakoram range are descending from their camps to help with search efforts, says Mingma Gyabu Sherpa, a Nepalese lawmaker. He's also a business associate of Nirmal Purja. Members of Imagine Nepal, a commercial mountaineering operator, are also helping out, he says. Earlier we reported that movement had been recorded on Purja's tracking device - Mingma Gyabu Sherpa has confirmed this to the BBC as well, though he adds that this movement was recorded in the tracking system yesterday. Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing What is Broad Peak? published at 04:42 BST 04:42 BST Image source, Getty Images Broad Peak in Pakistan is regarded as one of the more challenging mountains for expeditions, and is ranked as the world's 12th highest peak. It's summit is 8,047m (26,400ft) high. That is also where yesterday's avalanche occured, in the Karakoram range, according to Pakistani authorities. It is among 14 "death zone" peaks that Nirmal Purja climbed in just over six months in 2019. In 2022, Broad Peak was the subject of an eponymous Netflix film that told the story of how a Polish climber attempted the first winter ascent to the mountain's peak. Image source, International Space Station Image caption, Photo from the International Space Station shows Broad Peak as seen from space Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Nirmal Purja's tracker appears active - report published at 04:21 BST 04:21 BST The tracking device belonging to Nirmal Purja has reportedly been showing movement, according to a report by Nepali newspaper Kantipur. The device's position has been changing in the tracking system, Mingma Gyabu Sherpa, Nirmal Purja's business partner, told Kantipur. He also said that even though the avalanche happened in the day on Thursday, they only got detailed information of it in the evening. We'll bring you more updates as we get them. title: Nepali journalist Anup Ojha wins Developing Asia Journalism Award - The Kathmandu Post
description: Nepali journalist Anup Ojha wins Developing Asia Journalism Award  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Nepali journalist Anup Ojha, a correspondent for Agence France-Presse (AFP), has won second prize at the Developing Asia Journalism Awards (DAJA) 2026 for his report on Nepal’s use of artificial intelligence to strengthen landslide early warning systems. Ojha previously worked for The Kathmandu Post.

Ojha was recognised for his story, “Landslide-prone Nepal Tests AI-powered Warning System”, which examined Nepal’s efforts to deploy AI technology to predict landslides and provide at-risk communities with warnings during the monsoon season.

Organised by the Asian Development Bank Institute (ADBI), the awards honour journalism that sheds light on development challenges and innovative solutions across Asia. This year’s competition drew 79 entries from 17 countries, with a focus on how artificial intelligence is transforming economies, public services and daily life.

Ojha shared the second prize with Guinevere Latoza of the Philippine Centre for Investigative Journalism, whose investigation explored how the rapid expansion of data centres is affecting energy-burdened households in the Philippines.

The first prize was awarded jointly to Indonesian journalists Roni Satria of CNN Indonesia for “AI and Dietary Colonisation: When Nasi Uduk Is Considered a Sin” and Caecilia Mediana of Kompas for “Fate of Digital Platform Shadow Workers”. Khulan M. of Inside Mongolia received an honourable mention for “Can AI Strengthen Mongolia's Disaster Prevention?”

According to ADBI, the judging panel of journalists and researchers selected five winning entries. Each winner will receive a cash prize of $2,000, with the awards ceremony to be held online in August.

Ojha’s story highlighted both the promise and the challenges of applying AI in one of the world's most landslide-prone countries, where extreme monsoon rainfall, fragile terrain and climate change continue to increase disaster risks.
